chunks: And as for what was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Mansur who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Poultry was presented to us, slaughtered, and our family ate it.' He said: 'The people of Mecca do not see any harm in it.' I said: 'Then what do you say?' He said: 'The price is upon them.'

So it is assumed that it was slaughtered in the Haram (sanctuary), and the report does not specify whether it was slaughtered in the Hal (profane area) or the Haram. And if that is not explicit in its apparent meaning, and there are among the reports that contain the elaboration of its meaning, then taking it is preferable. And we have previously presented a portion of it, and it is sufficient, God willing.
And to further clarify that, what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating slaughtered poultry if it is unknown whether it was slaughtered in the Haram or Hal?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the general practice of the people of Mecca, who considered slaughtered poultry permissible regardless of location, and his specific juristic ruling that the buyer bears the cost, likely reflecting a precautionary financial compensation (kaffarah) for violating the sanctity of the Haram. This highlights the Shia methodological principle of preferring explicit, distinguishing reports over ambiguous ones when determining legal obligations, particularly regarding the sanctity of Mecca's boundaries.
